ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A uniform bar of mass $M$ and length $L$ has three notches along the bottom. The center notch is at the center of mass of the bar, and the other two notches are a distance of $\frac{L}{12}$ on either side of the center notch. The bar is placed on a fulcrum as shown. A mass $M$, equal to the mass of the bar itself, is hung a distance $\frac{L}{4}$ from the right edge of the bar. When an unknown mass $M'$ is hung a distance $\frac{L}{4}$ from the left edge of the bar, the system remains in static equilibrium. Calculate the unknown mass 
\[M'\] in terms of 
\[M\].

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there is a uniformly long rod placed horizontally, and the total length between the left and right ends is marked as L. There are three adjacent notches at the bottom of the long rod; the middle notch corresponds to the position of the rod's center of mass, and the distances from the left and right adjacent notches to the middle notch are both marked as L/12. The top end of the triangular support contacts the leftmost notch among the three notches. On the left side hangs an unknown mass M', whose suspension point is L/4 from the left end of the long rod; on the right side hangs mass M, whose suspension point is L/4 from the right end of the long rod. Reasoning: Take the center of mass of the long rod, that is, the middle notch, as the coordinate origin x=0. Since the support is at the left notch, the support position is x=-L/12. The position of the left mass M' is L/4 to the right from the left end, that is, relative to the center of mass x=-L/4; the position of the right mass M is L/4 to the left from the right end, that is, relative to the center of mass x=+L/4. The long rod's own gravity Mg acts at the center of mass x=0. Take moments about the support: the distance from M' to the support is |-L/4-(-L/12)|=L/6, on the left side of the support; the distance from the long rod's own gravity to the support is |0-(-L/12)|=L/12, on the right side of the support; the distance from the right mass M to the support is |L/4-(-L/12)|=L/3, on the right side of the support. Static equilibrium requires the counterclockwise moment to equal the clockwise moment, therefore M'g(L/6)=Mg(L/12)+Mg(L/3). Simplifying gives M'(L/6)=M(5L/12), so M'= (5/12)/(1/6) M = 2.5M.

method.method_draft: Use a direct torque balance about the fulcrum. First read the diagram: the triangular fulcrum contacts the left notch of the three bottom notches; the unknown mass M' hangs on the left side at L/4 from the left end, and the known mass M hangs on the right side at L/4 from the right end. From the text, the center notch is at the uniform bar's center of mass and the adjacent notches are L/12 apart, so the pivot is L/12 left of the bar's center. Set the bar center as x=0. Then the pivot is at x=-L/12, M' is at x=-L/4, the bar's weight M acts at x=0, and the right mass M is at x=+L/4. Compute moment arms about the pivot: M' has arm L/6 to the left; the bar weight has arm L/12 to the right; the right mass has arm L/3 to the right. Static equilibrium gives M'g(L/6)=Mg(L/12)+Mg(L/3), leading to M'=2.5M.

method.method_draft: Use the combined center-of-mass condition instead of writing separate torques. First read the diagram: the bar is supported at the left of the three central notches, while M' is hung near the left quarter point and M is hung near the right quarter point. Use a coordinate measured from the left end of the bar. From the text and image, M' is at x=L/4, the bar's own center of mass is at x=L/2, the right mass M is at x=3L/4, and the fulcrum is one notch spacing L/12 left of the center, at x=L/2-L/12=5L/12. For a body resting in equilibrium on a single fulcrum, the total center of mass must lie vertically above the fulcrum. ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, there is a uniformly long rod placed horizontally, and the total length between the left and right ends is marked as L. There are three adjacent notches at the bottom of the long rod; the middle notch corresponds to the position of the rod's center of mass, and the distances from the left and right adjacent notches to the middle notch are both marked as L/12. The top end of the triangular support contacts the leftmost notch among the three notches. On the left side hangs an unknown mass M', whose suspension point is L/4 from the left end of the long rod; on the right side hangs mass M, whose suspension point is L/4 from the right end of the long rod.

Reasoning: Take the center of mass of the long rod, that is, the middle notch, as the coordinate origin x=0. Since the support is at the left notch, the support position is x=-L/12. The position of the left mass M' is L/4 to the right from the left end, that is, relative to the center of mass x=-L/4; the position of the right mass M is L/4 to the left from the right end, that is, relative to the center of mass x=+L/4. The long rod's own gravity Mg acts at the center of mass x=0.

Take moments about the support: the distance from M' to the support is |-L/4-(-L/12)|=L/6, on the left side of the support; the distance from the long rod's own gravity to the support is |0-(-L/12)|=L/12, on the right side of the support; the distance from the right mass M to the support is |L/4-(-L/12)|=L/3, on the right side of the support. Static equilibrium requires the counterclockwise moment to equal the clockwise moment, therefore M'g(L/6)=Mg(L/12)+Mg(L/3). Simplifying gives M'(L/6)=M(5L/12), so M'= (5/12)/(1/6) M = 2.5M.
